abstract: Key-value caches in large-scale inference pipelines often suffer from head-of-line stalls when the working set exceeds the available memory. Aether-Cache introduces an information-theoretic compression layer that activates during a stall, applying run-length encoding to string values while preserving LRU semantics. The design guarantees lossless reconstruction, maintains a strict $O(N)$ forward and $O(N)$ inverse complexity, and incurs only O(|$\Sigma$|) auxiliary memory for the codebook. We formally prove a Shannon-entropy reconstruction invariant and provide a static AST analysis that confirms the algorithmic bounds. The implementation is fully Ruby-based and publicly available. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/ruby-algorithms-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261121_210255_aggron__aggressive_compression}
